s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory distress with a subcutaneous mass in the cervical region
salient_findings: Subcutaneous mass in the ventral cervical region
Mild leukocytosis with neutrophilia and lymphopenia
key_facts: 1-week history of dyspnea and inspiratory noise
Esophageal obstruction was suspected but not confirmed
Subcutaneous mass is 10 × 8 × 3-cm, partially firm and fluctuant, and mildly warm
No dysphagia, other masses, or lymphadenopathy were detected
Mild leukocytosis (23,690/µL) with neutrophilia (92.4%) and lymphopenia (3.0%)
Hematocrit was 39.8%, MCV was mildly increased, and MCHC was mildly decreased
Flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea showed no abnormalities
Cervical ultrasonography showed a well-demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass
Thoracic and cervical radiographs demonstrated a ventral soft-tissue-density mass in the mid-to-caudal cervical region

shortlist.label: Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous mass is partially firm and fluctuant, mildly warm, and painful, with mild leukocytosis and neutrophilia

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous mass is well-demarcated and encapsulated, with no intrinsic vascular flow, suggesting a benign tumor

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous mass in the cervical region, with no communication with the trachea or esophagus, and a well-demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic appearance on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous mass is partially firm and fluctuant, with a history of suspected esophageal obstruction, which could have led to trauma and bleeding

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mild leukocytosis and lymphopenia, with a subcutaneous mass in the cervical region, which could be a sign of lymphoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a subcutaneous mass that is partially firm and fluctuant, mildly warm, and painful, along with mild leukocytosis and neutrophilia, suggests an infectious or inflammatory process, which is most consistent with an abscess.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically non-painful, firm, and not fluctuant, which does not match the description of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Branchial cleft cyst
rejected.why: While branchial cleft cysts can present as neck masses, they are typically not painful or warm, and the presence of leukocytosis and neutrophilia suggests an infectious process rather than a congenital anomaly.

rejected.label: Hematoma
rejected.why: Hematomas are typically associated with a history of trauma, which is not mentioned in this case, and would not typically cause leukocytosis or neutrophilia.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would likely be associated with lymphadenopathy, which was not detected, and the presence of a single, well-demarcated mass is not typical of lymphoma.
